Review: Palworld ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Palworld is the game everyone joked about at first — “Pokémon with guns” — but it turned out to be so much more than that. It’s bold, fresh, and absolutely unafraid to take risks where Pokémon has played it safe. While Nintendo keeps polishing the same formula, Palworld kicks down the door and says: “What if you could build, survive, craft, and still have adorable creatures at your side?” And somehow… it works brilliantly.

Pros:

Fresh Take on the Monster Genre: For years Pokémon fans begged for innovation — open-world, survival, crafting — and Palworld just did it without hesitation. It feels like the evolution of the genre.

Building & Survival: Unlike Pokémon, you can actually live in this world. You farm, craft, build bases, and your Pals help you with real labor. It’s half survival sim, half creature adventure, and all addictive.

Freedom of Playstyle: Want to peacefully raise Pals on your farm? Go ahead. Want to fight, capture, and strap a rocket launcher to your best buddy? Also possible. That level of freedom is unheard of in Pokémon.

Co-op & Multiplayer: Exploring, battling, and building with friends is something Pokémon fans have dreamed of forever — Palworld just made it real.

Variety of Pals: They’re cute, they’re weird, they’re tough — and the fact that they’re useful for things like mining or building adds actual gameplay depth beyond just battling.

Community Love: Players adore how unapologetically wild it is, and it’s quickly built a cult following that sees it as the first real challenger to Pokémon’s throne.

Cons: (but forgivable)

Balance & Polish: Some mechanics feel rough around the edges (early access quirks), but nothing game-breaking.

Ethical “Dark Humor”: Yes, you can work your Pals pretty hard. Some players find it hilarious, others a little too edgy. But hey, that’s part of the game’s bold identity.

Performance: Depending on your setup, the game can run into frame dips or bugs. Nothing a patch can’t fix, but it’s noticeable.

Potential Legal Drama: Let’s be real — the Pokémon comparisons stirred up some controversy. Hopefully, Palworld keeps pushing forward without lawsuits slowing it down, because it truly deserves its own space.

Final Thoughts

Palworld is not just “Pokémon with guns.” It’s a daring, creative spin that finally gives fans the freedom and innovation they’ve wanted for years. Where Pokémon is cautious, Palworld is fearless. Where Pokémon repeats, Palworld experiments. It’s survival, crafting, creature collecting, and pure chaos wrapped into one — and right now, there’s nothing else like it on the market.

It’s brave, it’s fun, and it’s proof that the monster-collecting genre has so much untapped potential. Palworld is a one-of-a-kind experience that’s making history.

Reviewed by Zulandin from Zul TV on YouTube and TikTok

It's everything I could ask from a trainer game. The simple fact that I can pet my little critters puts this game leagues ahead of any competitor.

I like their animations, I love how expressive they all look while working, sleeping, eating, etc.
I like the open world and the fact I can explore it freely, no closed off area or anything.
I like the multiplayer mode, whether I'm working with friends or competing with them.
I love the pal exclusive abilities. I can ride around on a giant fat cat, jump off, throw my penguin as a grenade, and then finish the enemy off with my fox flamethrower. The way you can work with them is fun as hell.

And above all, I love the fact that I don't have to buy this game twice to have access to all pals. This company showed great respect for it's players and for that, I am grateful.
